Hi Mina / Marissa,

Thanks again for offering to help. Quick ask — we have rotating badge scanners at three entrances (north, south, demo hall). The vendor delivers separate CSV dumps for each scanner at end of day. We need a reliable procedure to: (1) dedupe leads across scanners, (2) attach the scanner origin and timestamp to the HubSpot contact as a custom event, and (3) ensure attendees have explicitly opted in with the event consent text before we sync to HubSpot/Salesforce.

Can Redwood advise on the best merge key (email vs badge_id vs phone) and the preferred place to store consent metadata so we can satisfy auditors? The team needs this in place by Monday morning to avoid a manual cleanup.

Appreciate any recommended playbook or a short checklist.

—Alex
Acme Retail, Event Ops

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear brief. High level plan below; I attached a CSV manifest and the suggested consent wording (docx):

1) Merge key recommendation: primary = email (when present), fallback = phone, final fallback = badge_id. We recommend email-first because it maps best to HubSpot and avoids splitting known contacts.

2) Duplicate resolution: ingest per-scanner CSVs into a short-lived staging table, run deterministic merge by (email -> phone -> badge_id) and source_rank (scanner priority: demo hall > north > south) so the most relevant scanner props win for fields like 'first_seen_location'. Keep a separate list of duplicates for audit.

3) Consent capture & retention: store the consent boolean and consent_text as event properties on the HubSpot contact (event: conference_opt_in) with timestamp and scanner_id. Keep raw scanner CSVs for 90 days in the shared Drive bucket; push only contacts with consent=true to HubSpot/Salesforce. That satisfies common audit expectations; legal can push for longer retention if required.

4) Field mapping: attach 'scanner_id','scanner_location','scan_timestamp','consent_text','consent_timestamp' as custom properties. Add a webhook that posts the merged contact to HubSpot via their Contacts API. For Salesforce, we map the same fields to a custom Lead object.

5) Rollback & alerts: If more than 5% of daily scans lack email/phone, auto-flag the batch and halt automated sync so ops can review.

Let me know if you want a runbook or I can walk your team through the staging->merge->sync job.

Mina Haddad
Field Marketing Ops, Redwood Inference

Adding technical detail for the ingest glue:

- Scanner CSV schema (attached) columns: badge_id, scanner_id, scanner_location, scan_timestamp (UTC), email, phone, raw_payload. We should normalize phone to E.164 during staging.
- HubSpot mapping (attached spreadsheet): create a single custom event 'edgecloud_scan' with properties described by Mina. For HubSpot dedupe we will upsert by email; if email absent, use phone. If both absent, create a ticket in 'manual-review' pipeline.
- If multiple scanners contain the same email on the same day, the scanner with higher source_rank wins for location fields; but we keep an array property 'scan_history' with a compact JSON string of prior scans for chain-of-custody.

Operational asks from my side: please confirm the scanner priority order and whether Acme wants our default 90-day raw retention or longer. Also confirm DocuSign or signed consent isn't required — the event-level consent_text should be sufficient.

Ben Carter
